minutes.headline: Select Board approved a Unitil pole petition and ratified two appointments; interim building commissioner resigned.
minutes.summary: The chair opened with a long personal statement about Lake Shirley and the lake improvement corporation, and a resident objected to waiving fees and allowing camping at special events. No budget decisions were made.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved a Unitil petition for a new utility pole at 994 Northfield Road as presented.
The board ratified two town manager appointments, a principal account clerk and a DPW facilities director; the minutes record the votes as not audible.
The board accepted the interim building commissioner's resignation; the minutes record the vote as not audible.
The town manager is weighing four ways to cover the building commissioner role, including regionalizing, a temp firm, per diem help, or a waiver for the local inspector.
A resident objected in public comment to waiving fees and allowing camping at special events on town property.

why_it_matters: Until the building commissioner role is filled, permit and inspection work depends on whichever arrangement the town manager chooses, which could affect how fast residents get approvals and what the town budget, mostly taxes, pays for coverage.
Fee waivers for special events on town property would shift utility and cleanup costs to the town budget, mostly taxes, and the board may be asked to set that policy.
watch_next: August 20th: the town's attorney is to meet the board in executive session on police union proposals.
Which option the town manager chooses to cover the building commissioner role.
